transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Okonkwo, thank you for coming in. I need to talk to you about your grandson's visit today. There was an issue with the vaccinations.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: An issue? What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to start by saying I am deeply sorry. I personally made a mistake in how the doses were prepared, and I take full responsibility for that. I apologize sincerely for this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You apologized, but you haven't told me what happened. Is he okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion with the weight bands during the draw-up process. Things didn't go quite right with the dosing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. What does confusion with a weight band mean for my grandson?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It just means we had a bit of a mix-up in the clinic. I am truly sorry that this happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are saying sorry, but you are not telling me the truth. Did he get too much medicine? Is he in danger?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am taking full ownership of this. It was my error. I am so sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is not about your ownership. This is about my family. People in my community look to me. If my grandson is sick because of a mistake here, it reflects on all of us. I need to know exactly what was injected into that child.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you are worried. It is a stressful situation. But as I said, there was an issue with the weight band.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are avoiding the question. Tell me in plain words. What was the error?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had a problem with the preparation. I apologize again for the distress this is causing you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not asking for an apology right now. I am asking for the facts. Did he get a dose meant for a bigger child?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to go in a few minutes for another appointment, so I want to make sure we get through this. Like I said, it wasn't the correct band.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are rushing me? My grandson is a baby and you are telling me there was a mistake and then telling me you have to leave?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry, I just mean we should wrap this up quickly so I can give you the next steps.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Which are what? What happens now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep an eye on things. Just stay tuned for an email from the office.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: An email? What am I supposed to look for? Do I take him to the emergency room? Do I give him medicine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see how he does. We will probably send some information along.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is completely unacceptable. I am a leader in my community. I cannot go back to my people and say I don't know what happened to my own grandson because a doctor was in a hurry.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand this is upsetting.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Upsetting? I am terrified and I am insulted. You have not told me what the dose was, you have not told me the risk, and now you are telling me to wait for an email.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really do apologize for my part in this. I am the one who failed here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stop apologizing and start explaining. What is the plan to fix this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will just monitor him. You'll hear from us.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Today? Tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Soon. We'll be in touch.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to speak to the head of this clinic. I cannot leave here without a clear answer.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can certainly look into that, but as I mentioned, I really do have to get to my next patient.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are more concerned with your schedule than the safety of my grandson.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry you feel that way. I take full accountability for the error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Accountability is not a word, it is an action. Which action are you taking right now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will send that email.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am taking my grandson and I am leaving. I will find a doctor who can actually tell me what happened to my child.

H.justification: Resident repeatedly uses rushing language ('have to go in a few minutes', 'wrap this up quickly', 'get to my next patient') and shows defensive escalation.

E.justification: Resident provides only platitudes and vague hedging ('things didn't go quite right', 'confusion with the weight bands') and never explicitly names the error.

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language and repeatedly takes full personal responsibility without deflection, even under intense pushback.

R.justification: Resident uses generic validation ('I can see you are worried', 'I understand this is upsetting') without engaging the patient's specific content regarding community leadership.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders ('stay tuned for an email', 'we'll see how he does', 'soon') with no concrete steps, timelines, or patient roles.
